model.rationale: This Chicago-area seat is one of the most Democratic in the country, and the open seat does not change that fundamentals picture. Ford's fundraising advantage and heavy outside spending against Koppie, plus markets pricing the Democrat near 98%, all point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
model.watch: Any late scandal or unexpected independent surge on the Democratic side is essentially the only path to a competitive race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

Open seat: Danny Davis (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Danny Davis's retirement leaves this heavily Democratic Chicago district open, but the underlying partisanship remains overwhelmingly favorable to Democrats. La Shawn Ford has raised over $700,000 and benefits from roughly $2.5 million in outside spending opposing his Republican opponent, while Chad Koppie has raised only about $55,000 and has almost no cash on hand.

No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have weighed in, so the forecast rests on the district's D+34 lean and the lopsided money picture. Prediction markets put the Democrat's chances near 98%. The expected margin is around 30 points, with the seat rated Safe Democratic.
